Thus, we reaffirm our decision in the Interim Report to 38 seek an alternative method to the SMSA approach.
Based on comments received both prior and subsequent to the Interim Report, the generally favored method of zone expansion is through adjustment of the populationmileage formula. The formula is a familiar concept to carriers and shippers; it is not, however, without its criticisms. Certain distortions are caused by the formula's sole reliance on central city population to determine commercial zone limits. The population statistics of record in this very proceeding reflect the fact that many cities are afflicted with population declines within their antequated political boundaries, while suburban economic development is thriving. In recognition of this fact, the Commission uses the largest decennial census figure for a particular municipality when computing zone limits under the formula, Commercial Zones and Terminal Areas, 115 M.C.C. 882, 887-88 (1972). While ameliorating this problem to a certain extent, we are aware that this practice does not provide a complete solution in some cases.
